scope: Proposition 8.1 (Dimension-parameterized success bound) of the manuscript “Subsphere methods for memory-sample lower bounds in noiseless Gaussian regression” (preprints/Subsphere-methods-for-memory-sample-lower-bounds-in-noiseless-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a645c0aa5ef45578), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants C ≥ 2 and d∗ such that the following holds for every integer d ≥ d∗. Set k = p = ⌊d/32⌋, γ = d/32. Let j ≥ 0 and m be integers with d/2 + 2j ≤ m ≤ d. Consider a fixed-length learner with jk independent exact Gaussian samples in dimension m, Borel rules, and at most 2d2 states at each layer. Its output may be any vector in Rm. Its rules may use arbitrary fixed parameters independent of the target. Its randomized experiment, initialization, any shared rule seed, and fresh randomness obey the joint measurability, independence, and information restrictions in Definition 1.1, with m in place of d. If the target s is uniform on Sm−1, then for every η > 0, P{∥output − s∥ ≤ η} ≤ (Cj+1 η)γ . (55)
